tools.description: Wrap layers into a new group layer (Figma-style), reparenting them while preserving their stage positions. Only the top-most selected layers are reparented; descendants of a selected parent ride along so internal nesting is kept. Returns the new groupId. Pair with set_motion_group_auto_layout to make the group reflow its children, or animate/transform the group as one unit.

tools.name: ungroup_motion_layers
tools.description: Dissolve one or more group layers, re-parenting their children to the group's parent (or the composition root) while preserving stage positions. The group layers themselves are removed.

tools.name: set_motion_group_auto_layout
tools.description: Turn a group into a Figma-style auto-layout frame: its children pack into a centered row (horizontal) or column (vertical) with a fixed gap, and re-pack automatically whenever a child's size changes. Pass direction (horizontal|vertical), gap (px, default 24), align (start|center|end, default center). Pass clear:true to remove auto-layout and free the children. Locked or position-keyframed children opt out of the flow and keep their own placement.

tools.name: precompose_motion_layers
tools.description: Pull the given layers into a new nested composition (a reusable 'component' / precomp) and replace them in place with a single composition layer that references it. Edit the component once and every instance updates. Use add_motion_component_instance to stamp more instances and set_motion_instance_overrides to vary text/color per instance. Returns the new componentId (nested composition id) and the precomp layerId.

tools.name: add_motion_component_instance
tools.description: Stamp another instance of a component: duplicate an existing precomp (composition) layer so it references the same master component. Editing the master updates every instance. The copy lands offset by offsetX/offsetY (default 48,48) and, if the source is inside a group, stays a sibling in that group. Returns the new instance layerId.

tools.name: set_motion_time_remap
tools.description: Time-remap a precomp (composition) layer — retime, freeze, reverse, or hand-key its source time. compositionLayerId must reference a layer with type 'composition'. Exactly one mode: `enable:true` lays down a linear identity remap (start of source -> end of source) so you can then adjust it; `reverse:true` plays the source backwards; `freeze:true` holds a single source frame (optional `freezeTime` seconds, default 0); `disable:true` clears the remap; or pass explicit `keyframes` as an array of { time, value, easing? } where time is the layer-local time and value is the source time (both seconds). Only one of enable/reverse/freeze/disable/keyframes may be provided.

tools.name: set_motion_instance_overrides
tools.description: Override text and/or color on individual child layers of a component INSTANCE, without touching the master component or its other instances. Pass overrides as an array of { childLayerId, text?, color? } where childLayerId is a layer id inside the master component. text applies to text children; color applies to text or shape children (a color override flattens a gradient fill to solid). An entry with neither text nor color clears that child's override. Pass clear:true to remove all overrides on this instance.

tools.name: disintegrate_motion_layer
tools.description: After-Effects-style disintegration: fade the target layer out while spawning a matching particle burst from its position (colored from its fill/text color), so it appears to crumble into dust. time (composition-absolute seconds, default = layer start) is when it disintegrates; duration (default 0.7s) is the fade length. The original layer is trimmed to end at the disintegration point. Pair with add_motion_cursor_click for a click-then-disintegrate beat. Returns the particle burst layerId.

tools.name: morph_motion_layers
tools.description: Morph one whole layer/view INTO another (After-Effects crossfade + transform tween): layer A fades out while layer B fades in starting from A's position/scale/rotation and settling into its own — so B appears where A was and animates into place. Use this to transition between two designed views/screens. Both layers must overlap the morph window (time..time+duration) or it no-ops and returns an error. For morphing a single SHAPE's outline into a different shape, use morph_motion_shape instead. fromLayerId, toLayerId; time (default 0), duration (default 0.6s).

tools.name: add_motion_cursor_click
tools.description: Drop an animated mouse cursor that travels to a target layer, click-presses on arrival, and makes the target react (a Click Press pulse) — the classic UI-demo 'a hand clicks the button' beat. The cursor is an image layer backed by a baked SVG pointer. targetLayerId; time (composition-absolute start, default 0), travel (seconds to reach the target, default 0.8), fromX/fromY (optional start point; defaults to up-and-left of the target). Returns the cursor layerId. Follow with disintegrate_motion_layer on the same target for click-then-disintegrate.

tools.name: import_image_layer
tools.description: Add a real image (logo/screenshot/icon) into a composition from a public URL or a data: URI. Downloads it into the media library, registers a composition image asset, and creates an image layer. Optional: name, x, y (pixel center), width, height, fit (contain|cover|fill), cornerRadius (rounded-rect clip — a cheap way to put a photo inside a rounded screen without a track matte), startTime (seconds, default 0), duration (seconds, default the composition duration), rotation (degrees), opacity (0-1). Returns data.layerId and data.assetId.

tools.name: add_motion_3d_object
tools.description: Add a TRUE 3D object (WebGL/Three.js under the hood) to a composition — it renders with real depth and rotates so every side is visible (unlike the 2.5D layers). `object` is one of box | rounded-box | sphere | cylinder | cone | torus | icosahedron | plane | phone (a full iPhone-style device with screen + camera plateau) | model (load ANY .glb/.gltf via modelUrl — auto-centered and scaled to fit) | text3d (extruded 3D text via `text`, with `extrude` depth). Declarative — you describe it, the engine does the WebGL. Optional: name, x, y (pixel center), width, height (render bounds), size/depth/aspect/cornerRadius (geometry), color, metalness (0..1), roughness (0..1), materialKind (physical|basic), emissive, mapAssetId (an image asset id to texture onto the phone screen, e.g. a wallpaper from import_image_layer), rotationX/Y/Z (initial degrees), fov, cameraDistance, environment (studio|dark|none — studio gives realistic reflections on metal/glass), groundShadow (true drops a soft contact shadow under the object), startTime, duration. Animate the spin with animate_layer property 'transform.rotation.y' (or .x/.z) — e.g. 0→360 over 4s shows the whole device turning in 3D. ZOOM/DOLLY: keyframe 'transform.position.z' — +1 pushes the camera 2x closer (zoom in), +2 = 4x, negative pulls back. Combine a position.z 0→1.5 ramp with a rotation.y tilt for a cinematic push-in.

tools.name: morph_motion_shape
tools.description: Animate a shape MORPHING into a different shape (After Effects-style path morph): the outline smoothly transforms, point-by-point, from one form to another. Give the source shape (layerId) and a target — toLayerId (morph into another shape layer's outline), toShapeType (rectangle|circle|ellipse|triangle|polygon|star|arrow|line, built at toWidth×toHeight, defaulting to the source size), or toPath (an explicit SVG path string centered at the origin — supply any custom outline, e.g. a logo or icon). Morph runs fromTime (default 0) → toTime with optional easing. Works between completely different shapes (arc-length resampling). Pair with a 'lift' — animate transform.position.z and transform.scale — to pop a button off a UI surface and then morph it into an icon.

tools.name: set_motion_shape_path
tools.description: Replace the whole outline of a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path'). points is an array of >=2 finite {x,y,inX?,inY?,outX?,outY?} vertices in layer-local pixel coordinates, where inX/inY and outX/outY are ABSOLUTE bezier control-handle coordinates (in = handle from the previous point, out = handle toward the next point); omit handles for straight corners. closed (default keeps the layer's current pathClosed) marks the path as a closed loop. The layer must have shapeType:'path' — create one via add_motion_layer with shapeType:'path'.

tools.name: edit_motion_shape_path_point
tools.description: Edit a single vertex (by index, 0-based) of a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path'). Pass x/y to move the anchor (its handles move with it), and/or inX/inY (incoming handle) / outX/outY (outgoing handle) as ABSOLUTE layer-local pixel coordinates. Supply at least one of x/y/inX/inY/outX/outY. Use insert_motion_shape_path_point / remove_motion_shape_path_point to change the point count.

tools.name: insert_motion_shape_path_point
tools.description: Insert a vertex into a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path') AFTER the given index (0-based). Pass an explicit point {x,y,inX?,inY?,outX?,outY?} (layer-local pixels, absolute handles) or omit it to insert a midpoint on the segment following afterIndex. Increases the point count by one.

tools.name: remove_motion_shape_path_point
tools.description: Remove the vertex at index (0-based) from a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path'). Refuses (INVALID_PARAMS) when the path is already at its minimum (2 points for an open path, 3 for a closed one).

tools.name: add_motion_shape_path_keyframe
tools.description: Add or replace a shape.pathData keyframe at a time on a bezier PEN shape layer (shapeType 'path') so its outline animates/morphs over time. Supply pathData (an SVG path string) or points (an array of >=2 {x,y,inX?,inY?,outX?,outY?} vertices, layer-local pixels, absolute handles); omit both to snapshot the layer's CURRENT path. easing is any known easing name. Re-calling at the same time replaces that keyframe.

tools.name: transform_motion_keyframes
tools.description: Batch-transform ALL keyframes of one property on a motion layer (the AE graph-editor keyframe ops). op is: 'reverse' (mirror values across the property's own time span), 'scale' (stretch/compress times about the first keyframe by factor scale>0 — 2 doubles the spacing), or 'duplicate' (copy every keyframe shifted by offset seconds, merging onto existing). scale is required for 'scale'; offset (may be negative) is required for 'duplicate'. property is any animatable id (transform.*, shape style properties like shape.width, shape.fill.opacity, effect.<id>.<param>, mask.<id>.<prop>, modifier.<id>.<prop>, ...) — note shape path data is not an animatable id here; animate a PEN path with add_motion_shape_path_keyframe. Use copy_motion_keyframes / paste_motion_keyframes to move keys between different properties. Any roving keyframes on the property keep constant-speed spacing: their times are re-derived from the surrounding anchors after the op, so reverse/scale/duplicate reposition them automatically.

tools.name: copy_motion_keyframes
tools.description: Read a motion layer property's keyframes into a portable clipboard payload (relative time offsets, values, and easings) for inspection or for feeding paste_motion_keyframes. Returns data.clipboard plus entryCount, span (seconds), and sourceProperty. NOT_FOUND if the property has no keyframes. The roving flag is not carried in the clipboard — pasted keyframes start non-roving, and on the destination property any existing roving keyframes re-derive their constant-speed times after the merge.

tools.name: paste_motion_keyframes
tools.description: Copy every keyframe from fromProperty and paste them onto toProperty of the SAME layer, preserving relative spacing and easing, shifted so the run starts at (fromProperty's first keyframe time + timeOffset seconds, default 0). Existing keyframes on toProperty are kept (pasted keys merge, replacing any at identical times). Both properties must be valid animatable ids. Pasted keyframes are never roving; any roving keyframes already on toProperty re-derive their constant-speed times after the merge. Use transform_motion_keyframes to reverse/scale/duplicate keys in place on a single property.

tools.name: add_motion_3d_scene
tools.description: Create ONE scene3d layer that is a FULL 3D WORLD — many objects sharing a camera, lights, and an optional room — instead of a single object. Declarative: you place objects in 3D and the engine does all the WebGL. This legacy-compatible tool now also creates semantic creation assets/objects plus a motion-scene3d render binding, so the scene remains editable in Motion Creator's Creation workspace. `objects` is an array; each entry: { kind (box|rounded-box|sphere|cylinder|cone|torus|icosahedron|plane|phone|model|text3d|soccer-ball|open-box|room), name, x,y,z (world position), rotationX/Y/Z (deg), scaleX/Y/Z, size, depth, aspect, cornerRadius, modelUrl (for model), text+extrude (for text3d), panelTexts (labels for soccer-ball), lidAngle (open-box, deg), color, metalness, roughness, materialKind, emissive, mapAssetId, opacity, key, objectId, partId, tags }. `camera`: { posX,posY,posZ, targetX,targetY,targetZ, fov, near, far }. `room`: { enabled, size, wallColor, floorColor } (camera flies in from the open +Z front). Optional environment (studio|dark|none), groundShadow. Then keyframe motion with animate_scene_camera + animate_scene_object. Returns layerId + render object ids plus semantic scene/object ids.

tools.name: add_scene_object
tools.description: Append one object to an existing scene3d layer (created by add_motion_3d_scene). Same fields as one entry of add_motion_3d_scene's `objects`. When the layer has a semantic creation binding, or can be recovered into one, this also appends an editable creation asset/object and render binding so Motion Creator can inspect and revise it later. Returns the render objectId plus semantic creation ids.

tools.name: set_motion_scene_object
tools.description: Statically edit one object inside a multi-object scene3d layer (created by add_motion_3d_scene). Merge only the fields you pass onto the object matched by objectId. transform: { position?{x,y,z}, rotation?{x,y,z} (deg), scale?{x,y,z} }. material: { color?, metalness?, roughness?, emissive?, emissiveIntensity?, opacity?, transmission? (0..1 glass), ior? (index of refraction), clearcoat? (0..1), clearcoatRoughness? (0..1), materialKind? (physical|basic), mapAssetId?, normalMapAssetId?, roughnessMapAssetId?, metalnessMapAssetId? } (metalness/roughness/opacity/transmission/clearcoat/clearcoatRoughness clamp to 0..1). geometry: { kind?(box|rounded-box|sphere|cylinder|cone|torus|icosahedron|plane|phone|model|text3d|soccer-ball|open-box|room), size?, depth?, cornerRadius?, aspect?, modelUrl? (for kind=model), text? (for kind=text3d), extrude? (text3d extrusion fraction), panelTexts? (string[] for soccer-ball) }. lidAngle? (deg, for kind=open-box) is set at the object level. For animated changes use animate_scene_object instead.

tools.name: remove_motion_scene_object
tools.description: Remove one object from a multi-object scene3d layer by objectId. Refuses to remove the last remaining object — delete the scene3d layer instead when you want an empty scene.

tools.name: set_motion_scene_camera
tools.description: Set the static (non-animated) cinematic camera on a scene3d layer. position?{x,y,z}, target?{x,y,z}, fov? (degrees), near? (near clip plane distance), far? (far clip plane distance). Only the fields you pass change. Complements animate_scene_camera, which keyframes the camera over time.

tools.name: animate_scene_camera
tools.description: Keyframe the cinematic camera of a scene3d layer — the 'camera at this angle at this time, move this way, orbit this point' control. `position` and `target` are arrays of { time, x, y, z, easing }; `fov` is an array of { time, value, easing }. Times in seconds. Re-calling replaces the camera keyframes. When the layer is bound to an editable creation scene, this also mirrors the camera animation into creation animation state for recovery and later editing. Example fly-in then orbit: position [{time:0,x:0,y:4,z:24},{time:1.4,x:0,y:2,z:9},{time:2.4,x:7,y:2,z:7},{time:6,x:-7,y:2,z:7}], target locked on the subject.

tools.name: set_model_animation
tools.description: Bind a GLB/glTF animation clip to a model inside a scene3d layer so Motion Creator renders the rigged model over time instead of as a static pose. Use clipName or clipIndex to choose a clip; omit both to use the first clip. timeOffset shifts the clip start, playbackRate changes speed, and animationLoop=false clamps on the final frame. For multi-object scenes pass objectId; for a legacy single-model scene3d layer omit objectId.

tools.name: animate_scene_object
tools.description: Keyframe one object inside a scene3d layer in TRUE 3D over time — shake, spin, lift, open. `position`, `rotation` (degrees), `scale` are arrays of { time, x, y, z, easing }; `opacity` and `lidAngle` (open-box) are arrays of { time, value, easing }. Times in seconds. Re-calling replaces that object's keyframes for the channels you pass. When the layer is bound to an editable creation scene, this also mirrors position/rotation/scale/opacity tracks into creation animation state for recovery and later editing. Example lift: position [{time:1.4,x:0,y:0,z:0},{time:2.4,x:0,y:5,z:0}] + rotation spin [{time:1.4,x:0,y:0,z:0},{time:6,x:0,y:720,z:0}].

tools.name: animate_motion_layers
tools.description: Apply an animation preset to MANY layers at once with a per-layer stagger — e.g. 'stagger all the cards in with a slide-up'. presetId is one of fade-in, fade-out, slide-up-in, slide-left-in, scale-pop, rotate-in, pulse, float-loop, stroke-draw-on, stroke-pop, gradient-sweep, corner-bloom (see get_capabilities motion.animationPresets). Optional: startTime, duration, stagger (seconds added per layer in layerIds order), distance, intensity. Layers that don't support a shape-only preset are skipped.

tools.name: execute_action
tools.description: Escape hatch: dispatch any underlying editor action by type + params. Use get_capabilities and the action catalog for valid types.

tools.name: batch_actions
tools.description: Dispatch a sequence of raw actions in order; stops on first failure.

tools.name: export_motion_video
tools.description: Render a motion composition to a finished video file and return the filename plus width/height/duration/framesRendered and the format actually encoded. format: 'mp4' (H.264, opaque), 'webm-alpha' (VP9 with transparency), or 'mov-prores4444' (ProRes 4444 with transparency); default 'mp4'. On the web build only the desktop app can produce transparent WebM or ProRes — for those formats on web the export normalizes to opaque H.264, so you MUST pass acknowledgeH264Fallback:true to consent (otherwise the export fails with a warning telling you to acknowledge or use desktop). Optional filename overrides the auto-generated name. Inspect data.normalizedToH264 / data.encodedFormat to see what was really written. Expensive — requires confirmation.

tools.name: queue_motion_render
tools.description: Add a motion composition to the render queue for later batch export. format: 'mp4' | 'webm-alpha' | 'mov-prores4444' | 'png-sequence' (default 'mp4'). Optional rangeStart/rangeEnd (seconds, within the composition duration, start<end) render only that span; resolutionScale (1 | 0.5 | 0.25) downscales the output; optional filename overrides the auto name. On the web build transparent WebM and ProRes normalize to opaque H.264 — for those you MUST pass acknowledgeH264Fallback:true to consent (png-sequence is transparent but ZIP-encoded and never needs acknowledgement). Returns data.itemId. Use run_motion_render_queue to render.

tools.name: run_motion_render_queue
tools.description: Render every queued (or previously failed) item in the motion render queue sequentially and return per-item outcomes (data.outcomes: itemId, status, encodedFormat, filename, error). Items whose cancel was requested are skipped as 'canceled'. Expensive — requires confirmation.

tools.name: list_motion_render_queue
tools.description: List the current motion render queue items (data.items with itemId, compositionId, format, status, progress, and any range/resolutionScale/filename/error).

tools.name: cancel_motion_render_item
tools.description: Cancel a queued or in-progress motion render queue item by itemId. A queued item is canceled immediately; a rendering item stops at the next frame boundary. Returns whether the item was found.

tools.name: get_project_manifest
tools.description: Return the exact openreel-multicam/v1 manifest for a camera group, including participants, camera subjects, sync reference, and hard constraints.

tools.name: get_activity_map
tools.description: Read the reusable .orma speech activity map for an optional millisecond range. Large maps are deterministically sampled to at most 2,000 points.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Read optional per-participant local Whisper transcript segments from the separate .orma artifact.

tools.name: set_edit_policy
tools.description: Re-plan the automatic multicam edit from cached analysis. All values are schema-validated and manifest shot constraints remain hard bounds.

tools.name: annotate_segment
tools.description: Attach a concise planning note to a bounded multicam time range without modifying cached analysis.

tools.name: get_edit_summary
tools.description: Summarize shots, layouts, pending cut review, annotations, and top deterministic social candidates.

tools.name: override_cut
tools.description: Accept, reject, nudge by at most 2 seconds, or assign a valid manifest camera to one generated cut.

tools.name: preview_frame
tools.description: Render a frame at a bounded millisecond time for visual inspection of the current multicam edit.

tools.name: export_video
tools.description: Render the whole project to a video file and wait for it (use queue_export for long or queued jobs). With no options it writes a standard MP4 (H.264). Call get_export_options first for anything else: format (mp4|mov|webm|mxf), codec, bitDepth (8|10), hdr (sdr|pq|hlg), width, height, frameRate, bitrateKbps, audioChannels (mono|stereo|5.1), timecode, presetId. outputPath (absolute, inside the allowed folders; see get_app_state mcp.allowedRoots) puts the file there, overwrite:true replaces an existing one; without it the file stays in the app's export folder and data.path says where. targetLufs (-40..-5) normalizes loudness with a true-peak ceiling (truePeakCeilingDb, default -1). An unsupported combination returns UNSUPPORTED with a hint listing valid alternatives. Result data: path, filename, bytes, sizeBytes, sha256, format, contentType. Expensive: requires confirmation.

format.description: Container. Call get_export_options for what this machine can write.

presetId.description: A preset id from get_export_options presets[]. Explicit fields below override it.

bitDepth.description: 10 needs a codec that carries it (see get_export_options).

hdr.description: sdr (default), pq (HDR10 / ST 2084) or hlg. HDR is 10-bit H.265 (or ProRes 4444 XQ on desktop).

bitrateKbps.description: Video bitrate in kbps. Ignored by ProRes, DNxHR and the broadcast codecs, which are profile-rated.

maxBitrateKbps.description: Peak video bitrate cap in kbps. Switches to one-pass variable-bitrate rate control: bitrateKbps is the average, this the cap (desktop encoders apply both; the browser encoder applies the average only). Must be at least bitrateKbps.

rateControl.description: quality (default) = constant quality; vbr = one-pass, hit bitrateKbps on average; vbr2 = true two-pass VBR (desktop app, H.264 / H.265 only, slower: the frames are analysed, then encoded; not with a Rec.2020 sequence or HDR; clips under ~10 s can overshoot the target by 6-7 %). Implied by maxBitrateKbps.

bitrateMode.description: Shorthand for the rate control: cbr = hold bitrateKbps (peak cap equals the target), vbr1 = one-pass VBR, vbr2 = two-pass VBR (desktop, H.264 / H.265). Uses bitrateKbps as the target and maxBitrateKbps as the peak cap.

timecode.description: Write the sequence start timecode (MOV / MXF, desktop).

targetLufs.description: Normalize the mix to this integrated loudness (-40..-5).

outputPath.description: Absolute destination file, inside the allowed folders (Settings > MCP). Omit to keep the app's own output file.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at outputPath (default false).

tools.name: export_audio
tools.description: Render the project audio to a local file (format: mp3|wav|aac|flac|ogg, default wav) and return its local result metadata. Optional targetLufs (-40..-5) normalizes the mix to that integrated loudness with a true-peak ceiling (truePeakCeilingDb, default -1). Expensive — requires confirmation.

tools.name: ripple_delete_clip
tools.description: Delete a clip (or clipIds) and close the gap. Linked clips (separated audio/video) are deleted with it when the editor's linked selection is on (linkedClipIds overrides). Sync Lock: every other unlocked sync-locked track loses the same range and shifts earlier with it if that range is empty there; otherwise the edit is blocked and the error names the track (turn its Sync Lock off with set_track_sync_lock, or move its content). Tracks with Sync Lock off are untouched. One undo step.

tools.name: track_select_clips
tools.description: Premiere's Track Select Forward/Backward: the clip with clipId plus every clip and overlay item after it (direction "forward", default) or before it ("backward") on all unlocked tracks, or only on its own track with trackOnly. Items on locked tracks are never included. Read-only; pass the returned ids to ripple_delete_clip, delete or move tools to act on the whole range as one undo step.

tools.name: trim_edit_point
tools.description: Trim-mode nudge of one edit point by whole frames, like selecting it in the timeline and pressing , or . (1 frame) or Shift , / . (5). clipId + edge ("left" = the clip start, "right" = its end) name the edit point; frames > 0 moves the edge later in time, < 0 earlier. kind "roll" moves the cut between two touching clips (total length unchanged), "ripple" trims the one edge and pulls everything after it along; the default is roll at a cut and ripple at a free edge, and roll on a free edge falls back to ripple. Sync Lock, linked clips (pass linkedClipIds to override), locked tracks and source handles apply exactly as for the Ripple and Roll tools; the move is clamped to the handles and the applied frames are returned. One undo step.

tools.name: delete_gap
tools.description: Ripple-delete the empty gap on a track that contains `time` (seconds, or timeFrame in frames): later clips move earlier to close it. Space after the last clip is not a gap. Sync Lock: every other unlocked sync-locked track must be empty over the gap and shifts with it; otherwise the edit is blocked and the error names the track. Locked tracks block it. One undo step.

tools.name: set_track_target
tools.description: Turn a track's target toggle (the V1/A1 buttons) on or off. Targeted tracks are what Extract, Lift, Add Edit, Paste, Match Frame and insert/overwrite use when no trackId is given. Editor state, not part of the project (no undo step). Live editor only.

tools.name: set_source_patch
tools.description: Patch a Source monitor component to a timeline track: kind video|audio, trackId of a video/image track (video) or an audio track (audio), or null to clear (auto). insert_from_source / overwrite_from_source then place the source's video and audio on the patched tracks (two linked clips when both are patched to different tracks). Editor state, not part of the project (no undo step). Live editor only.

tools.name: add_edit
tools.description: Premiere-style Add Edit: split every clip under a timeline time on trackIds (default: the targeted tracks, else every unlocked track). One undo step. Give `time` seconds or `timeFrame`.

tools.name: open_in_source_monitor
tools.description: Load a library media item into the Source monitor (the Source tab beside Program), optionally parked at `time` seconds. Does not edit the project. Live editor only.

tools.name: set_source_in_out
tools.description: Set or clear the Source monitor In and/or Out marks of a media item (seconds, or inFrame/outFrame). Pass null to clear a mark. Marks persist per media item and are used by insert_from_source / overwrite_from_source. Not a timeline edit (no undo step). Live editor only.

tools.name: insert_from_source
tools.description: Premiere-style Insert (ripples later content) from the Source monitor using three-point editing. The source range is the media's In/Out marks (set_source_in_out; or pass sourceIn/sourceOut; unmarked = whole media). Placement: at `at` (default 0), or at the sequence In when sequenceIn/sequenceOut are given: source In-only fits the range (Out derived), source Out-only back-times, source In+Out with only sequenceOut ends at it; with all four marks the source range wins at sequenceIn. component: both (default) | video (muted) | audio. One undo step. Returns the rule applied.

tools.name: overwrite_from_source
tools.description: Premiere-style Overwrite (replaces what it covers) from the Source monitor using three-point editing. The source range is the media's In/Out marks (set_source_in_out; or pass sourceIn/sourceOut; unmarked = whole media). Placement: at `at` (default 0), or at the sequence In when sequenceIn/sequenceOut are given: source In-only fits the range (Out derived), source Out-only back-times, source In+Out with only sequenceOut ends at it; with all four marks the source range wins at sequenceIn. component: both (default) | video (muted) | audio. One undo step. Returns the rule applied.

tools.name: roll_trim
tools.description: Roll the cut between a clip and its neighbour: one clip gets longer by exactly as much as the other gets shorter, so total duration and everything else stay put. Uses the clip's source handles; clamped to them. One undo step. Positive moves later in time. Give delta in seconds or deltaFrame in project frames (snapped to the frame grid and clamped to the available source handles; the applied value is returned). Linked clips (separated audio/video) are edited together automatically when the editor's linked selection is on; pass linkedClipIds ([] for none) to override (they must share this clip's timing).

edge.description: Which cut to roll: "right" (default) = the cut at the clip end, "left" = the cut at its start.

tools.name: slide_trim
tools.description: Slide a clip along the timeline between its two neighbours without changing its own content or the overall duration: the previous clip's out and the next clip's in move with it. Needs an adjacent clip on both sides. One undo step. Positive moves later in time. Give delta in seconds or deltaFrame in project frames (snapped to the frame grid and clamped to the available source handles; the applied value is returned). Linked clips (separated audio/video) are edited together automatically when the editor's linked selection is on; pass linkedClipIds ([] for none) to override (they must share this clip's timing).

tools.name: rate_stretch
tools.description: Rate Stretch: change a clip's length by dragging one edge so its playback speed changes to fill the new length (source range unchanged); never ripples. Returns the new speed. Not available on clips with speed ramps, images or generated media. One undo step. Positive moves later in time. Give delta in seconds or deltaFrame in project frames (snapped to the frame grid and clamped to the available source handles; the applied value is returned). Linked clips (separated audio/video) are edited together automatically when the editor's linked selection is on; pass linkedClipIds ([] for none) to override (they must share this clip's timing).

tools.name: make_split_edit
tools.description: Offset a linked clip pair's edit points like Premiere's J-cut and L-cut. kind "l" = L-cut: the audio cut falls `frames` AFTER the picture cut (audio trails over the next shot); kind "j" = J-cut: the audio cut falls `frames` BEFORE it (audio leads into the shot). Give a clip at the cut (video or audio) and which edge is the cut (default: the edge a neighbouring clip touches). Only the audio side moves (side "video" moves the picture instead); at a cut between two clips that track rolls across it, at a clip end it trims/extends. The linked pair stays linked. The offset is measured from the other side's cut, so repeating the call is a no-op. Clamped to the available source handles, gaps, locked tracks and one-frame minimum; the applied value and the limit hit are returned. Default 12 frames. One undo step.

tools.name: extend_edit
tools.description: Premiere's Extend Edit: move the edit point (the head or tail) of the given clips to a timeline time, on the picture, the sound or both (side). At a cut between two clips it rolls the cut; at a clip end it trims or extends into free space. Linked partners of the given clips are included. Each clip is clamped independently by its own source handles, so the sides can land at different times; the applied value per clip is returned. Give `time` seconds or `timeFrame`. One undo step.

tools.name: insert_media
tools.description: Premiere-style Insert: place library media at a timeline time on the main track (V1/A1 unless trackId is given), splitting what is underneath and rippling every unlocked track later by the clip length. One undo step. Give `at` seconds or `atFrame`. Optional sourceIn/sourceOut select the source range.

tools.name: overwrite_media
tools.description: Premiere-style Overwrite: place library media at a timeline time on the main track (V1/A1 unless trackId is given), replacing whatever it covers on that track without moving anything else. One undo step. Give `at` seconds or `atFrame`. Optional sourceIn/sourceOut select the source range.

tools.name: lift_range
tools.description: Premiere-style Lift: remove everything inside [start, end] on the unlocked tracks (or only trackIds), leaving a gap. Clips straddling the range are split. One undo step. Give start/end in seconds or startFrame/endFrame.

tools.name: extract_range
tools.description: Premiere-style Extract: remove everything inside [start, end] on trackIds (default: the targeted tracks, else every unlocked sync-locked track) and close the gap by rippling later content earlier. Clips straddling the range are split. With explicit/targeted tracks, every other unlocked sync-locked track must be empty in the range (it then shifts too); otherwise the edit is blocked and the error names the track. One undo step. Give start/end in seconds or startFrame/endFrame.

tools.name: add_edit_all_tracks
tools.description: Split every clip under a timeline time on all unlocked tracks at once (Premiere's Add Edit to All Tracks). One undo step. Give `time` seconds or `timeFrame`.

tools.name: match_frame
tools.description: Find the source media and source timecode shown at a timeline time: of clipId, or of the topmost visible video clip at `time`. Returns mediaId, source time and timecode so the same frame can be located in the library and used for insert_media/overwrite_media sourceIn. Also selects the source media in the library (as the UI does). Does not edit the project.

tools.name: detect_scenes
tools.description: Scene edit detection: analyse a video clip's footage for hard cuts and return them (source and timeline times, score). Does not edit anything; follow with apply_scene_cuts using the returned analysisId. sensitivity 0..1 (default 0.5; higher finds more cuts), minSceneLength in seconds (default 1). Needs the live editor with the source media loaded; reversed clips are unsupported.

tools.name: apply_scene_cuts
tools.description: Apply the cuts from detect_scenes as one undo step: splitClip splits the clip (and its linked clips) at every cut, addMarkers drops a timeline marker at each. At least one must be true. Clips with speed ramps or freeze frames can only get markers.

tools.name: open_scopes
tools.description: Open the Scopes panel (waveform = luma, parade = RGB parade, yc = luma + chroma, vectorscope, hls = hue/saturation polar plot, histogram) and optionally pick the kind. scale ire|pq|hlg sets the waveform level axis (nits for HDR footage); falseColor true/false toggles the IRE-band exposure overlay on the Program monitor (preview only, never exported). Use get_scope_stats to read the numbers. Live editor only.

tools.name: close_scopes
tools.description: Close the Scopes panel. Live editor only.

tools.name: get_scope_stats
tools.description: Read what the scopes show as numbers for the current program frame (the preview as rendered, effects and grade included): luma min/max/average/median and 1st/99th percentile, black and white clipping percent (overall and per RGB channel), average/max saturation, dominant hue (degrees, name, share), colour cast (vectorscope Cb/Cr) and plain-language warnings. Use it for colour QA before and after grading. Seeks the playhead first when `time` is given. Works whether or not the panel is open. Live editor only.

tools.name: list_pro_effects
tools.description: List the pro video effects (blurs, keys, colour tools, distortions, stylize and generator effects: e.g. camera-blur, tilt-shift, luma-key, color-key, spherize, twirl, corner-pin, lens-flare, strobe-light; pass effectType to filter and see every type) with each parameter's range, default and neutral (no-op) value. Add one with add_video_effect {effectType, params}; omitted params take the defaults. Read-only.

tools.name: add_hsl_secondary
tools.description: Add a Lumetri-style HSL Secondary to a clip: a qualifier (hueMin/hueMax/hueSoft in degrees, satMin/satMax/satSoft and lumMin/lumMax/lumSoft in percent, denoise 0-100, blur 0-20 px, invert) keys a matte, and the correction (temperature, tint, contrast, sharpen, saturation -100..100, wheelX/wheelY -1..1) applies only inside it. Optional maskShape none|ellipse|rectangle with maskX/maskY/maskW/maskH (percent), maskFeather (px), maskInvert limits the matte. Pass `sample` {r,g,b} (0-255) to key around a colour like the eyedropper. A clip can carry several secondaries (applied in stack order). Params are the hsl-secondary pro-effect params (see list_pro_effects); omitted params are neutral (saturation 0). One undo step. Returns effectId; refine with set_secondary_qualifier; keyframe with add_keyframe property fx:<effectId>:<param> using the returned effectId (e.g. fx:<effectId>:saturation), which animates that secondary independently of any others.

tools.name: set_secondary_qualifier
tools.description: Change the qualifier / matte settings of an HSL secondary: explicit fields (hueMin, hueMax, hueSoft, satMin, satMax, satSoft, lumMin, lumMax, lumSoft, denoise, blur, invert) and/or eyedropper `sample` {r,g,b} (0-255) with mode set (default: a new range around the colour), add (widen the key to include it) or subtract (narrow the key to drop it); explicit fields win over the sample. Reads the secondary's current range first, so add/subtract compose. One undo step.

tools.name: grab_still
tools.description: Grab the graded Program frame (at `time` seconds, default the playhead) as a still and make it the comparison reference. Stills live in the editor session only (not in the project). Use toggle_comparison to show it against the current frame. Live editor only.

tools.name: toggle_comparison
tools.description: Show or hide the Program monitor comparison view (preview only; never affects export or scopes). With no arguments it toggles. mode: off | side (side by side) | split-v (draggable vertical wipe) | split-h (horizontal wipe); reference: bypass (the ungraded frame), still (stillId from grab_still) or playhead (a frame pinned at refTime seconds); split 0..1 positions the wipe. Live editor only.

tools.name: set_clip_mask_path
tools.description: Create or edit a free-form Bezier mask on a clip (the same data the Program-monitor pen tool draws). points are in composition space 0..1 (x right, y down), at least 3; each may carry absolute handleIn / handleOut {x,y} (a point with no handles is a sharp corner). Omit maskId to add a new closed 'drawn' mask; pass maskId to edit one. With timeSeconds the path is written as a path keyframe at that timeline time (all keyframes of one mask must keep the same point count and the mask then interpolates between them); otherwise it replaces the static path. Optional feathering (0..100), expansion (-100..100), opacity (0..1), inverted. Optional combine (add|subtract|intersect|difference, default intersect) sets how this mask combines with the masks listed before it on the clip; the first mask ignores it. One undo step.

tools.name: export_timeline_xml
tools.description: Serialize the video/audio timeline for another editor and return the file text. format "xmeml" (default) = Final Cut Pro 7 XML v5 that Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve import; "fcpxml" = Final Cut Pro X FCPXML 1.10; "edl" = CMX3600, one file per video track; "otio" = OpenTimelineIO JSON (Resolve, Avid, Premiere plugins; also carries sync lock and track targeting). Clips, tracks, speed, opacity, volume, cross dissolves and markers are included. Pass "sequence" (id or name, see list_sequences) to export ANY sequence, open or not; it defaults to the active one. Nested sequences stay nested in xmeml (nested sequence), otio (stacks) and fcpxml (compound clips / ref-clip); edl gets them flattened, with a report entry. Multicam cuts are written as multiclip (xmeml) or mc-clip (fcpxml) with every angle; otio and edl flatten them to the active angle, with a report entry. Everything dropped or approximated (effects, speed ramps, text clips, sync lock where the format has no field...) is listed per clip in `report.items`, never silently; `report.notes` says AAF is available only from File > Export timeline in the editor (it is a binary file, so this text tool does not return it; see docs/interchange.md). Read-only.

sequence.description: Sequence id or name to export; defaults to the active sequence.

tools.name: import_timeline_xml
tools.description: Import a Final Cut Pro XML (xmeml, from Premiere/Resolve/FCP7), FCPXML, OpenTimelineIO (.otio JSON) or CMX3600 EDL sequence passed as `xml` text (the OTIO JSON or EDL text goes in the same argument). An EDL carries no frame rate: pass `frameRate` (default 24, or 29.97 for drop frame); each clip keeps its reel and source timecodes in metadata.edl, and reels are relinked to bin media by reel name (the media embedded start timecode decides the in-point; when several files share a reel name the source timecode picks one). Media is relinked to the media bin by filename; files not in the bin become offline placeholders and are listed in `unmatched`. mode "replace" (default) swaps video/audio tracks and markers (text/graphics tracks stay); "append" adds the imported tracks. Nested sequences (xmeml clipitem sequences, otio stacks, fcpxml compound clips) become project sequences with nest clips, and xmeml multiclips become multicam sources with their angles. One undo step. Pass dryRun:true to only report what would be imported.

tools.name: add_track_audio_effect
tools.description: Add an effect to a track's (or the master bus's) audio effect rack. Racks hold up to 5 effects processed in order, in live playback and in export. effectType: gain|eq|compressor|limiter|reverb|delay|noiseReduction|deHum|deClick|deClip|deEss|deReverb|gate|brickwallLimiter|lowPass. Optional params (omitted ones use defaults; gain: gainDb -24..24 dB; eq: lowGain -24..24 dB, midGain -24..24 dB, midFreq 200..8000 Hz, midQ 0.1..10, highGain -24..24 dB; compressor: threshold -60..0 dB, ratio 1..20 :1, attack 0.001..1 s, release 0.01..3 s, knee 0..40 dB, makeupGain 0..24 dB; limiter: ceiling -24..0 dB, release 0.01..1 s; reverb: roomSize 0..1, damping 0..1, wetLevel 0..1, dryLevel 0..1; delay: time 0..2 s, feedback 0..0.95, wetLevel 0..1; noiseReduction: threshold -60..0 dB, reduction 0..1, attack 0..100 ms, release 0..500 ms; deHum: frequency 40..70 Hz, harmonics 1..8, q 5..100, depth 0..1; deClick: sensitivity 0..1, maxWidth 2..48 smp; deClip: threshold -24..0 dBFS, maxRun 4..120 smp; deEss: frequency 2500..12000 Hz, bandwidthQ 0.3..6, threshold -60..0 dB, ratio 1..20 :1, attack 0.0002..0.05 s, release 0.005..0.5 s, listen 0..1; deReverb: amount 0..1, rt60 0.1..3 s, floor -40..0 dB; gate: threshold -80..0 dB, range -80..0 dB, attack 0.0002..0.2 s, hold 0..1 s, release 0.01..2 s; brickwallLimiter: ceiling -24..0 dBTP, release 0.01..1 s; lowPass: frequency 100..20000 Hz, slope 12..48 dB/oct), position (0-based slot, default end) and bypassed. Returns the new effectId. One undo step.

target.description: Track id, bus id (create_bus), or "master" for the master bus.

tools.name: set_track_audio_effect_param
tools.description: Edit one effect in a track/master audio rack: any of params (object of numeric parameters, clamped to range; gain: gainDb -24..24 dB; eq: lowGain -24..24 dB, midGain -24..24 dB, midFreq 200..8000 Hz, midQ 0.1..10, highGain -24..24 dB; compressor: threshold -60..0 dB, ratio 1..20 :1, attack 0.001..1 s, release 0.01..3 s, knee 0..40 dB, makeupGain 0..24 dB; limiter: ceiling -24..0 dB, release 0.01..1 s; reverb: roomSize 0..1, damping 0..1, wetLevel 0..1, dryLevel 0..1; delay: time 0..2 s, feedback 0..0.95, wetLevel 0..1; noiseReduction: threshold -60..0 dB, reduction 0..1, attack 0..100 ms, release 0..500 ms; deHum: frequency 40..70 Hz, harmonics 1..8, q 5..100, depth 0..1; deClick: sensitivity 0..1, maxWidth 2..48 smp; deClip: threshold -24..0 dBFS, maxRun 4..120 smp; deEss: frequency 2500..12000 Hz, bandwidthQ 0.3..6, threshold -60..0 dB, ratio 1..20 :1, attack 0.0002..0.05 s, release 0.005..0.5 s, listen 0..1; deReverb: amount 0..1, rt60 0.1..3 s, floor -40..0 dB; gate: threshold -80..0 dB, range -80..0 dB, attack 0.0002..0.2 s, hold 0..1 s, release 0.01..2 s; brickwallLimiter: ceiling -24..0 dBTP, release 0.01..1 s; lowPass: frequency 100..20000 Hz, slope 12..48 dB/oct), bypassed and position (new 0-based slot: reorders the rack). Also sets the bus fader/pan of that track: volume (linear 0..4, 1 = 0 dB) and pan (-1..1; tracks only) when effectId is omitted. One undo step.

target.description: Track id, bus id (create_bus), or "master" for the master bus.

tools.name: remove_track_audio_effect
tools.description: Remove one effect from a track's (or the master bus's) audio effect rack by effectId. One undo step.

target.description: Track id, bus id (create_bus), or "master" for the master bus.

tools.name: set_track_automation
tools.description: Replace one automation lane of an audio track: lane "volume" (linear gain 0..4, 1 = 0 dB) or "pan" (-1 left .. 1 right), points [{time (timeline seconds), value}]. The lane replaces the track fader / pan while it plays, in preview and in export. An empty array clears the lane. Read the current lanes from the track's automation field. One undo step.

tools.name: create_bus
tools.description: Add a submix bus to the Audio Track Mixer. Tracks route into it with set_track_output (or send to it with add_send); it has its own effect rack/fader (set_track_audio_effect_param with target = the bus id), mute/solo and automation, then plays into the master or another bus (output; loops are refused). role: general|dialogue|music|effects. With preset "stems" it instead creates the Dialogue / Music / FX buses and routes tracks by role/name. Returns busId. One undo step.

output.description: Bus id this bus plays into; omit or "master" for the master.

tools.name: update_bus
tools.description: Edit a bus: name, role, muted, solo, output (another bus id or "master"; loops are refused) and/or volume automation points [{time (timeline s), value (linear gain 0..4)}] (empty array clears). Fader and effects use set_track_audio_effect_param / add_track_audio_effect with target = the bus id. One undo step.

tools.name: remove_bus
tools.description: Delete a bus. Tracks and buses that played into it are re-routed to its own output (or master) and sends to it are removed, all in one undo step.

tools.name: set_track_output
tools.description: Assign a track's main output to a bus (busId) or back to the master (busId omitted or "master"). Sends are separate (add_send). One undo step.

tools.name: add_send
tools.description: Add an aux send from a track to a bus. level is linear 0..4 (1 = 0 dB, default 1). preFader true taps before the track fader (ignores it), false (default) after it. Both respect track mute/solo. At most 6 sends per track, one per bus. Returns sendId. One undo step.

tools.name: set_send_level
tools.description: Edit one send (trackId + sendId): level (linear 0..4), preFader, muted and/or automation points [{time (timeline s), value (linear 0..4)}] that replace the level while they play (empty array clears). removeSend true deletes the send. One undo step.

tools.name: export_stems
tools.description: Export each bus (or the busIds given) as its own WAV stem in one go. A stem is the bus's post-fader output (its rack, fader, automation and everything routed or sent into it) over the whole timeline, before the master rack, so stems line up and re-sum. bitDepth 16 or 24 (default 24). Needs the live editor; the files are handed to the user (downloads). Read-only for the project.

tools.name: measure_loudness
tools.description: Measure real loudness per ITU-R BS.1770-4 / EBU R128: integrated LUFS (gated), loudness range (LU, EBU Tech 3342), true peak (dBTP, 4x oversampled) and sample peak. scope "timeline" (default) renders the whole mix offline exactly as an export would (optional startTime/endTime in seconds); scope "clip" measures one clip (clipId) as it currently sounds, in isolation; scope "bus" measures one bus's stem (busId: its post-fader output including everything routed or sent into it). Read-only. Silence reports integratedLufs null.

tools.name: normalize_clip_loudness
tools.description: Measure a clip's integrated loudness (BS.1770-4) and set its clip gain so it lands on targetLufs (default -14; common targets: -14 streaming, -16 podcast/social, -23 EBU R128 broadcast). Clip gain is capped at +12 dB; the result says when the cap stopped it and where the true peak ends up. One undo step. Clips with volume automation have that automation scaled instead.

tools.name: list_color_library
tools.description: List the user's saved looks (named full Lumetri grades) and imported LUTs. These live outside the project, so they are reusable across projects. Read-only.

tools.name: save_look
tools.description: Save a clip's complete Lumetri grade (wheels, curves, hue curves, HSL, tone, white balance, vignette, creative LUT and Input LUT) as a named look in the user's library. Fails when the clip has no grade. Does not change the project.

tools.name: apply_look
tools.description: Apply a saved look (by id or name) to one or more clips (clipIds), replacing their whole grade with the look's. One undo step for all clips.

tools.name: delete_look
tools.description: Delete a saved look from the user's library (by id or name). Clips already graded with it keep their grade.

tools.name: save_clip_lut_to_library
tools.description: Store the LUT currently applied to a clip (slot creative, the default, or input) in the user's LUT library under `name`, so it can be reused on other clips and projects. Does not change the project.

tools.name: apply_library_lut
tools.description: Apply a LUT from the library (by id or name) to one or more clips. slot "creative" (default) is the look LUT after the grade; slot "input" is the Input LUT applied to the source before the whole grade (e.g. camera log to Rec.709). Optional intensity 0..1. One undo step.

tools.name: remove_clip_lut
tools.description: Remove the creative or Input LUT (slot) from one or more clips. One undo step.

tools.name: export_lut_cube
tools.description: Export the LUT applied to a clip (slot creative, the default, or input) as an Adobe/Resolve .cube file. The intensity is baked in unless bakeIntensity is false. Live editor only (it downloads the file).

tools.name: get_caption_transcript
tools.description: Read the caption transcript: words with start/end seconds and speakers, plus sentences (word index ranges) and the caption tracks. Words of cues without word timings carry estimated:true. Optional captionTrackId ("" = default track), speaker filter, and limit/offset over words (default 400). Read-only; use it to pick the times for transcript_cut_range.

tools.name: export_captions
tools.description: Render the project's captions as a file: format srt, vtt (WebVTT with <v Speaker> voice tags), ttml (TTML/IMSC1), scc (Scenarist CEA-608: pop-on, odd-parity byte pairs, EOC on the cue start frame, 32-column rows, <i>/<u> as mid-row codes) or stl (EBU-STL, binary: returned as data.contentBase64). One caption track per call (captionTrackId, "" = default; omit for every cue). includeSpeakers prefixes SRT cues with "Name: ". SCC/STL options: frameRate (SCC default 29.97 drop-frame, STL default 25), dropFrame (SCC), offsetSeconds (programme start, e.g. 3600), title (STL). SCC/STL return data.issues, the validation report (wrapped lines, rows dropped, characters substituted, captions delayed because the 608 channel was busy). embedded: "subtitle" or "cea608" instead returns data.embedded, the subtitle track a video export would embed (webvtt/mov_text/c608 payload text and warnings) for context mp4|mov (container) and desktop:true|false; pass those to queue_export captions to embed. Read-only.

tools.name: caption_qc
tools.description: Quality-check the captions: reading speed (characters/second and words/minute), rows per cue, characters per row, minimum/maximum duration, gaps shorter than minGapFrames frames and overlaps. Defaults: maxCps 17, maxWpm 180, maxLines 2, maxCharsPerLine 42, minDuration 0.833s, maxDuration 7s, minGapFrames 2, frameRate = the project's. One caption track via captionTrackId ("" = default). Returns data.issues (code, severity, cueId, cueIndex, time in seconds to jump to, message, value, limit), data.counts, data.averageCps, data.worstCps. Read-only: fix problems with the caption edit tools.

tools.name: import_captions
tools.description: Add captions from SRT, WebVTT (speakers from <v Name> tags), SCC (Scenarist CEA-608: pop-on, paint-on and roll-up RU2/3/4 on CC1; frameRate default 29.97, drop-frame detected from the timecode separator), a word-timed transcript JSON ({segments:[{start,end,speaker?,words:[{word,start,end}]}]}) given as content, or an EBU-STL file given as contentBase64. For SCC/STL, offsetSeconds is subtracted from every time (the file's programme start) and styleTags:"keep" keeps <i>/<u> for italic/underlined runs. Optional captionTrackId and language put them on their own caption track (e.g. a translation). SCC/STL decoding notes come back in data.issues. One undo step.

tools.name: rename_speaker
tools.description: Rename a speaker on every caption (renaming onto an existing speaker merges them; an empty `to` clears the label). One undo step.

tools.name: transcript_cut_range
tools.description: Ripple-cut a time range [start, end] (seconds, as read from get_caption_transcript) out of the sequence the way deleting that text in the Transcript panel does: every unlocked sync-locked track is cut and closed together (linked picture and sound stay in sync), markers and captions ripple, one undo step. Fails (nothing changes) if a linked partner sits on a locked or not sync-locked track.

tools.name: remove_filler_words
tools.description: Find filler words in the transcript (default list: um, umm, uh, uhh, uhm, er, erm, hmm, like, you know; override with fillers) and ripple-cut each one out, all as ONE undo step. Pass preview:true to only list what would be removed (text, start, end) without editing. Same sync-lock and linked-clip rules as transcript_cut_range.

tools.name: remove_pauses
tools.description: Ripple-cut pauses longer than minDuration seconds between spoken words, leaving `keep` seconds (default 0.2) of breathing room at each, all as ONE undo step. preview:true lists them without editing.

tools.name: set_text_scroll
tools.description: Make a text clip roll (vertical credits) or crawl (horizontal ticker) across the frame over its whole duration. Pass { clipId, scroll: { mode: "roll"|"crawl", direction?: roll up|down, crawl left|right, startOffscreen?: true, endOffscreen?: true } } or scroll:null to stop scrolling. With startOffscreen the text enters fully outside the frame, with endOffscreen it leaves fully outside; a side that is not off-screen rests at the clip's position. Rendered the same in preview and export (2D text only: 3D-extruded or 3D-rotated titles ignore it).

tools.name: set_caption_style
tools.description: Style caption cues as ONE undo step. Targets subtitleIds, else every cue of captionTrackId, else all cues. `style` merges into each cue's style: fontFamily, fontSize, color, backgroundColor, position (top|center|bottom), highlightColor, strokeColor, strokeWidth, shadowColor, shadowBlur, shadowOffsetX, shadowOffsetY, boxPaddingX, boxPaddingY, boxRadius, safeMargin (0..0.25 of the frame; keeps captions inside the safe area). `cueSettings` merges WebVTT settings (line, snapToLines, lineAlign, position, positionAlign, size, align) and is written into VTT export; SRT cannot carry them. cueSettings:null clears them.

tools.name: list_saved_styles
tools.description: List the saved text styles and caption styles stored on the project (id, name).

tools.name: save_text_style
tools.description: Save a text clip's look under a name so it can be applied to other text clips. Pass { name, clipId } (copies that clip's style and scroll) or { name, style } with a TextStyle object. Saving an existing name overwrites it.

tools.name: save_caption_style
tools.description: Save a caption look (style plus cue settings) under a name. Pass { name, subtitleId } to copy a cue's look, or { name, style, cueSettings? }. Saving an existing name overwrites it.

tools.name: apply_saved_style
tools.description: Apply a saved style (id or name) to text clips ({ kind: "text", styleId, clipIds }) or caption cues ({ kind: "caption", styleId, subtitleIds }) as ONE undo step. Use list_saved_styles to see what exists.

tools.name: delete_saved_style
tools.description: Delete a saved text or caption style by id or name. Clips that already use it keep their look.

tools.name: list_bins
tools.description: List the Project panel's bins (nested folders) with their ids, paths, label colours and item counts, plus how many media items sit at the project root.

tools.name: create_bin
tools.description: Create a bin (folder) in the media library, optionally inside another bin ("parent": id or name) and optionally filling it with existing media ("mediaIds") like "New bin from selection". One undo step.

name.description: Bin name; made unique among siblings if it already exists.

parent.description: Parent bin id or name; omit or "root" for top level.

mediaIds.description: Media to move into the new bin.

label.description: Label colour id or name: violet, iris, caribbean, lavender, cerulean, forest, rose, mango, purple, blue, teal, magenta, tan, green, brown, yellow; "none" clears it.

tools.name: move_to_bin
tools.description: Move media items (and/or whole bins) into a bin, or back to the project root ("bin": "root" or omitted). Bins cannot be moved into themselves. One undo step.

binIds.description: Bins to move (nest) into the destination.

bin.description: Destination bin id or name; "root" for the top level.

tools.name: rename_bin
tools.description: Rename a bin. One undo step.

tools.name: delete_bin
tools.description: Delete a bin together with its nested bins, every media item inside, and the timeline clips that use that media. Pass confirm:true to proceed; without it the tool only reports what would be deleted. One undo step restores everything.

tools.name: set_label
tools.description: Set the label colour of media items, timeline clips and/or bins. Label colour id or name: violet, iris, caribbean, lavender, cerulean, forest, rose, mango, purple, blue, teal, magenta, tan, green, brown, yellow; "none" clears it. For clips "inherit" goes back to following the media's label. Labels show as colour chips in the Project panel and as clip colour on the timeline. One undo step.

label.description: Label colour id or name: violet, iris, caribbean, lavender, cerulean, forest, rose, mango, purple, blue, teal, magenta, tan, green, brown, yellow; "none" clears it.

tools.name: set_media_log
tools.description: Edit the Project panel logging columns on media items: "scene", "shot", "take" (free text, "" clears), "goodTake" (boolean flag), plus "comment" and "description" (the log note). Applies to every id in mediaIds. One undo step.

tools.name: find_media
tools.description: Search the media library across every Project panel column (name, label, type, codec, comment, description, scene, shot, take, good take, ...). Every space-separated term must match; "scene:12" / "good:yes" / "take:2" limit a term to one column. "column" limits the whole search to one column (name, label, type, duration, frameRate, resolution, codec, audio, fileSize, startTimecode, importedAt, usage, comment, description, scene, shot, take, goodTake).

tools.name: list_smart_bins
tools.description: List the saved searches (smart bins) with their query, column and the live number of matching media items.

tools.name: create_smart_bin
tools.description: Save a search as a smart bin: a bin with no media of its own whose contents are the library items matching "query" (optionally limited to one "column"), recomputed live whenever metadata changes. One undo step.

tools.name: delete_smart_bin
tools.description: Delete a smart bin by id or name. Only the saved search is removed; no media is deleted. One undo step.

tools.name: make_subclip
tools.description: Create a subclip: a media-bin item that references a window (inPoint..outPoint, seconds or frames) of an existing video/audio item and is used like any media (drag, insert, overwrite). "restrictTrims": true keeps later trims on its clips inside the window. Omitting inPoint/outPoint uses the Source monitor marks for that media. One undo step.

bin.description: Destination bin id or name; defaults to the parent's bin.

tools.name: interpret_footage
tools.description: Override how video media is read. frameRate conforms the footage to that rate (a 30 fps file read as 24 fps plays at 0.8x and runs 25% longer); clips already on the timeline are retimed (speed and duration, later clips on the same track ripple to follow; pass retimeClips:false to change only the media item) and clips placed afterwards use it. pixelAspectRatio (0.25-4; 1.3333 for HDV 1440x1080, 0.9091 for DV NTSC) stretches the frame to its display width in preview, the Program monitor, scopes and export, so fit/fill math uses the display size. fieldOrder (progressive, upper, lower) marks interlaced footage, which preview and export deinterlace with the deinterlace mode (none, blend (default), bob). The file's own pixel aspect / field order are auto-detected when the importer can read them and show in list_media. Fields you give are merged into the item's existing interpretation (others are kept); clear:true goes back to what the file says. One undo step.

tools.name: list_sequences
tools.description: List the project's sequences (timelines) with id, name, canvas settings, duration, which one is active (the one every other tool edits), which have an open tab, and how many times each is nested in other sequences.

tools.name: create_sequence
tools.description: Create a new sequence and open it (it becomes the active timeline). Give "name" and optional "width", "height", "fps", "sampleRate" (default: the current sequence's settings), or "fromMediaId" to match a media item's size and frame rate with that clip placed at 0 (New Sequence From Clip). Pass "activate": false to leave the current sequence open. One undo step.

tools.name: open_sequence
tools.description: Open a sequence (id or name) in its own tab and make it the active timeline: every later edit, preview and export acts on it. Use to edit inside a nest ("clipId" of a nest clip also works). Undoing steps back to the previously open sequence.

tools.name: nest_clips
tools.description: Nest the given items (clip ids from list_clips on the active sequence; text/shape/sticker/SVG overlay and adjustment-layer ids also work) into a new sequence and replace them with one nest clip over the same span (Premiere's "Nest..."). Linked audio, transitions between the nested clips, masks, keyframes, effects, and the captions and markers inside the span travel with them. Optional "name". Editing inside the nest later updates every instance. Refused when a selected track is locked or the nest would overlap other clips. One undo step.

tools.name: list_graphic_templates
tools.description: List Essential Graphics templates (built-in lower thirds, titles, callouts, end cards, plus the user's saved ones) with their exposed controls (id, label, type, default, range), the protected intro/outro length and layers, and the graphics already placed on the active timeline. Filter with "category" (lower-third, title, callout, end-card, custom). Use the control ids with insert_graphic_template and set_template_parameter.

tools.name: insert_graphic_template
tools.description: Place an Essential Graphics template on the active timeline as ONE graphic (its layers are grouped). "templateId" is an id or name from list_graphic_templates. "startTime" (seconds, default 0) and optional "duration" (default: the template length; never shorter than its intro+outro). "values" sets exposed controls by id, e.g. {"name":"Alex Morgan","accent":"#ff6600","showTitle":false}. Optional "trackId"; otherwise a free graphics track is reused or created above the video. Returns the graphic id for set_template_parameter. One undo step.

tools.name: set_template_parameter
tools.description: Change exposed controls of a placed graphic. "graphicId" comes from insert_graphic_template / list_graphic_templates. Give either "parameterId" + "value" or "values" ({id: value, ...}) to set several at once in one undo step. Text controls take strings, color controls #hex / rgba(), slider/number controls numbers (clamped to the range), checkbox controls true/false (shows or hides a layer), position controls {"x":960,"y":540} in 1920x1080 design pixels.

tools.name: save_graphic_template
tools.description: Save a placed graphic (with its current control values as the new defaults, its edited layers and controls) as a reusable template in the user's library, listed by list_graphic_templates under category "custom". "graphicId" is the placed graphic, "name" the new template name. Does not change the project (no undo step). The user can export it as a .openreel-template file from the Inspector.

tools.name: set_sequence_frame_size
tools.description: Change the active sequence frame size ("width", "height" in pixels). By default ("scaleGraphics" true) every graphic template, text, shape and SVG clip of the sequence is rescaled so it keeps its proportion to the frame (a 1080p title stays inside a 640x360 frame); pass "scaleGraphics": false to change only the canvas. One undo step. Use update_project_settings for fps/sample rate.

tools.name: list_multicam_sources
tools.description: List the project's multi-camera sources (synced angles, numbered 1-9 like the number keys) and the multicam clips of the active sequence that use them, with each clip's active angle.

tools.name: create_multicam
tools.description: Create a synced multi-camera source from 2 to 9 video media items ("mediaIds", the first is the sync reference; angle numbers follow the order) and, by default, place it on the timeline at "startTime" (seconds, default 0) as one multicam clip showing angle 1. "syncMethod": "audio" (default: cross-correlates the cameras' audio, accurate to well under a frame; needs a host that can decode audio, or pass "offsets"), "timecode" (pass "timecodes": start timecode seconds per media), "in-points" (pass "inPoints": In time in each media), "markers" (pass "markers": a marker time in each media), or "manual" (pass "offsets": shared-time seconds at which each media's time 0 plays). "audio": {"mode":"follow"} (default: audio follows the video angle) or {"mode":"fixed","angle":N}. Pass "place": false to only create the source. One undo step. Then use switch_angle / record_multicam_cuts / flatten_multicam.

tools.name: switch_angle
tools.description: Switch a multicam clip to another angle, keeping every frame in sync. Identify the clip by "clipId" or by "atTime" (timeline seconds: the multicam clip on screen then). "angle" is the 1-based angle number (the number key), id or name. Refused when the angle has no footage for that span. One undo step.

tools.name: record_multicam_cuts
tools.description: Cut a multicam clip between angles in one pass, like pressing the number keys during playback: "cuts" is a list of {time (timeline seconds), angle (1-based number, id or name)}; each angle runs until the next cut, the last until "endTime". Splits the multicam clips where a cut lands inside them. One undo step for the whole pass.

tools.name: flatten_multicam
tools.description: Flatten multicam clips to their active angle: every cut becomes a plain clip of that angle (same frames, same audio), no longer linked to the multicam source. Optional "sourceId" or "clipIds" limit what is flattened. One undo step.

tools.name: render_in_to_out
tools.description: Render the timeline's In/Out range (or the whole sequence when none is marked) into the preview render cache so effects, transitions and grades play back at full frame rate. Optional rangeStart/rangeEnd (seconds, start<end) render that span instead. Frames already cached are skipped. Returns data.status (completed|canceled|failed), framesRendered, framesSkipped, elapsedMs and the codec. Not an edit: no undo step. Expensive — requires confirmation.

tools.name: delete_render_files
tools.description: Delete every cached preview render (Sequence > Delete render files). Playback of those segments goes back to live rendering. Cancels a running render first. Returns data.removedFrames. The project is unchanged: no undo step.

tools.name: get_render_status
tools.description: Report the render-status bar: data.segments lists timeline stretches as cached (green: plays from the render cache), light (yellow: needs a render but likely plays in real time) or heavy (red: effects-heavy, unlikely to play in real time); plain media is omitted. Also data.cachedRanges (seconds), frameCount, bytes and whether a render is running. Read-only.

tools.name: get_export_options
tools.description: List what export_video and queue_export can do on this machine, from the same sources as the Export dialog: formats[{id, container, codecs, bitDepths, hdr[sdr|pq|hlg], available, reason?, codecOptions, unavailableCodecs}], presets[{id, label, kind, format, codec, width, height, frameRate, bitrateKbps}] (pass an id as presetId), resolutions, frameRates, audioLayouts (mono|stereo|5.1), hdr {supported, reason?} and timecode {supported}. Call this before exporting anything but a plain MP4: an unsupported combination is refused with UNSUPPORTED and a hint that lists the valid alternatives. Read-only.

tools.name: queue_export
tools.description: Add a video export to the export queue (Export dialog > Add to queue) and, unless start=false, start the queue. The job captures the project as it is now: later edits do not change it. Give a quick preset id (mp4 | 4k | 1080p-high | 1080p-60) or explicit format (mp4|webm|mov), codec, width, height, frameRate and bitrate (kbps); anything omitted comes from the project. Optional rangeStart/rangeEnd (seconds, start<end) export only that span; filename overrides the output name; sequenceId renders that sequence instead of the active one (see list_sequences); usePreviews (default true) reuses frames from the preview render cache when it matches the export size and frame rate; smartRender (default true) stream-copies untouched, GOP-aligned runs of H.264 sources (also HEVC on desktop's native encoder) when codec, size and frame rate match the source and re-encodes everything else (finished jobs report 'Smart render: N% copied' in data.jobs[].smartRender, with reasons when less was copied). captions: [{captionTrackId ("" = default), burnIn (default true: draw the track into the picture), embedded: none|subtitle|cea608}] sets per-track caption delivery - "subtitle" embeds a subtitle track (WebVTT in browser MP4, tx3g mov_text in desktop MP4/MOV) and "cea608" embeds CEA-608 as a c608 track in desktop MOV (MP4 falls back to tx3g); a track with burnIn false is left out of the picture (smart render may then stream-copy under it). Jobs run one at a time. Also takes the export_video options: presetId (any id from get_export_options), codec incl. prores/dnxhr/xdcamhd422/avcintra100, format mxf, bitDepth, hdr (sdr|pq|hlg), audioChannels, timecode, targetLufs and outputPath (absolute, inside the allowed folders; overwrite:true replaces a file): when the job completes the file is placed there and list_export_jobs reports outputPath, outputBytes and sha256. An unsupported combination returns UNSUPPORTED with a hint. Returns data.jobId; poll list_export_jobs. Not an edit: no undo step. Expensive - requires confirmation.

presetId.description: A preset id from get_export_options presets[]. Explicit fields below override it.

bitDepth.description: 10 needs a codec that carries it (see get_export_options).

hdr.description: sdr (default), pq (HDR10 / ST 2084) or hlg. HDR is 10-bit H.265 (or ProRes 4444 XQ on desktop).

bitrateKbps.description: Video bitrate in kbps. Ignored by ProRes, DNxHR and the broadcast codecs, which are profile-rated.

maxBitrateKbps.description: Peak video bitrate cap in kbps. Switches to one-pass variable-bitrate rate control: bitrateKbps is the average, this the cap (desktop encoders apply both; the browser encoder applies the average only). Must be at least bitrateKbps.

rateControl.description: quality (default) = constant quality; vbr = one-pass, hit bitrateKbps on average; vbr2 = true two-pass VBR (desktop app, H.264 / H.265 only, slower: the frames are analysed, then encoded; not with a Rec.2020 sequence or HDR; clips under ~10 s can overshoot the target by 6-7 %). Implied by maxBitrateKbps.

bitrateMode.description: Shorthand for the rate control: cbr = hold bitrateKbps (peak cap equals the target), vbr1 = one-pass VBR, vbr2 = two-pass VBR (desktop, H.264 / H.265). Uses bitrateKbps as the target and maxBitrateKbps as the peak cap.

timecode.description: Write the sequence start timecode (MOV / MXF, desktop).

targetLufs.description: Normalize the mix to this integrated loudness (-40..-5).

outputPath.description: Absolute destination file, inside the allowed folders (Settings > MCP). Omit to keep the app's own output file.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at outputPath (default false).

tools.name: list_export_jobs
tools.description: List the export queue: data.jobs with id, outputName, sequenceName, presetLabel, status (queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|interrupted), progress (0..1), elapsedMs, etaMs, range, usePreviews, framesFromCache, smartRender ({copiedPercent, summary, reasons} once finished), error and outputPath (desktop). Read-only.

tools.name: cancel_export_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running export job by jobId (from queue_export / list_export_jobs). A queued job is dropped from the line; a running job stops at the next frame. Finished jobs are left as they are. Not an edit: no undo step.

tools.name: export_image_sequence
tools.description: Render frames of the project as numbered PNG or JPEG files delivered as one zip and wait for it. format png (default, lossless) | jpg, quality 1-100 (jpg only), width/height (default the project's), rangeStart/rangeEnd (timeline seconds, end exclusive; default the whole timeline) and pattern (file name with a zero-padded counter, e.g. 'frame_{0000}' -> frame_0042.png; default frame_{0000}), startNumber (added to the project frame index; default 0). One file per project frame, at most 5000 frames and about 1 GB: use a range for longer timelines. Result data: path, filename, bytes, frames, format. Not an edit: no undo step. Expensive: requires confirmation.

rangeStart.description: Start of the span to export, in timeline seconds (default 0). Pass together with rangeEnd.

rangeEnd.description: End of the span (exclusive), in timeline seconds. Must be after rangeStart.

outputPath.description: Absolute destination file, inside the allowed folders (get_app_state mcp.allowedRoots). Omit to keep the app's own output file; data.path says where.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at outputPath (default false).

tools.name: export_gif
tools.description: Render the project (or a span) as an animated GIF and wait for it. fps 1-50 (default 15; GIF delays are whole centiseconds, so the real rate is 100/round(100/fps), e.g. 15 -> 14.29, and frames are sampled at that rate so the duration stays true), width/height (default the project's size scaled to at most 640 wide), maxColors 2-256 (one global palette, default 256), loop 0 = forever (default) | n = n plays | 'none' = play once, rangeStart/rangeEnd (timeline seconds, end exclusive). Limits: 4096 px a side, 1500 frames and about 768 MB of frame pixels. Result data: path, filename, bytes, frames. Not an edit: no undo step. Expensive: requires confirmation.

rangeStart.description: Start of the span to export, in timeline seconds (default 0). Pass together with rangeEnd.

rangeEnd.description: End of the span (exclusive), in timeline seconds. Must be after rangeStart.

outputPath.description: Absolute destination file, inside the allowed folders (get_app_state mcp.allowedRoots). Omit to keep the app's own output file; data.path says where.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at outputPath (default false).

tools.name: import_media_from_path
tools.description: Import local video, audio, image and camera RAW files into the media library by absolute path. `paths` takes files and/or folders (folders import their media files; recursive:true includes subfolders). Every path is checked against the allowed folders (Settings > MCP; get_app_state lists them): symlinks are resolved, so a link that leaves an allowed folder is refused. Optional: copyToProject (desktop: also copy into the project's Media folder, originals untouched), ingestPreset none|proxies|copy for this import, createProxies (build preview proxies), bin (bin id or name to file the items in). Returns data.imported[{mediaId, path, name, kind video|audio|image|raw, durationSec, width, height, frameRate, codec}] and data.skipped[{path, code NOT_FOUND|OUTSIDE_ALLOWED_ROOTS|UNSUPPORTED_TYPE|UNREADABLE, message}]; use a mediaId with add_clip. Requires an open project (create_project first). Can take a while for big folders.

tools.name: open_project_file
tools.description: Open a saved project file (.oreel, .openreel or .json) by absolute path and make it the active project, replacing whatever is open now (the current project is saved first, so nothing is lost). The path must be inside the allowed folders (Settings > MCP; get_app_state lists them). Offline media shows as relinkable; use import_media_from_path to bring files back.
