Destructive to the open project's session state: requires confirmation.

path.description: Absolute path of the project file

tools.name: save_project_as
tools.description: Write the active project to a project file at an absolute path (.oreel or .openreel) and make that file the project's save target, so later saves update it. The path must be inside the allowed folders (Settings > MCP). An existing file is not replaced unless overwrite:true. Requires an open project. Unlike save_project (which only keeps the app's autosave), this produces a file you can hand back or reopen with open_project_file.

tools.name: import_timeline_from_path
tools.description: Import a timeline file by absolute path: Final Cut Pro XML (xmeml, from Premiere / Resolve / FCP7), FCPXML, OpenTimelineIO (.otio) or AAF. format "auto" (default) detects it; naming a format that does not match the file is an error. EDL files cannot be imported (export xmeml, FCPXML or OTIO instead). Media is relinked to the media bin by filename (import_media_from_path first); files not in the bin become offline placeholders listed in `unmatched`. mode "replace" (default) swaps video/audio tracks and markers, "append" adds the imported tracks. dryRun:true only reports. The path must be inside the allowed folders. One undo step. Replaces the timeline in replace mode: requires confirmation.

path.description: Absolute path of the timeline file

tools.name: get_app_state
tools.description: Report what OpenReel is doing right now, without needing its window: appVersion, platform, route (welcome|editor|...), windows {editor, count}, projectOpen and projectId, onboarding {status unseen|in-progress|done|skipped, path, skippedBy}, ai {configured, provider}, and mcp {toolCount, autoAllow, allowedRoots, protocolVersion}. mcp.allowedRoots are the folders the path tools (import_media_from_path, open_project_file, save_project_as, export outputPath) may read and write. Call this first in a session; it works with no project open. Read-only.

tools.name: dismiss_onboarding
tools.description: Dismiss OpenReel's first-run onboarding (the welcome path chooser and any open setup sheet) so it never covers the UI during an agent session. Idempotent: calling it again, or after the user finished onboarding, changes nothing. It does not touch any project and is never required before other tools. Lesson and AI-setup progress is kept.

tools.name: get_project_fonts
tools.description: List every font family used by text clips, motion-graphics text layers and caption styles, with where it is used and how it travels when the project is packaged (Collect Files). status is one of: embedded (user font copied into the package; license fsType installable/editable), embedded-readonly (fsType preview&print: embedded for preview/export, not for editing), restricted (fsType forbids embedding; not copied, install it on the other machine), unknown-license (font file license unreadable, e.g. WOFF2 uploads, or file data unavailable; not copied: re-upload as TTF/OTF/WOFF to embed), web (catalog font recorded by family + url, not copied), bundled (ships with OpenReel), system (installed OS font; cannot be embedded). Read-only; works only in the live OpenReel app.

tools.name: create_proxies
tools.description: Queue background builds of low-resolution H.264 proxies for video media (Project panel > Proxies > Create proxies). mediaIds picks items (default: every video without a proxy); quality is low (up to 540p), medium (720p, default) or high (1080p); force rebuilds an existing proxy. Jobs run one at a time in the background with progress in the Project panel and survive a reload; each finished proxy is linked to its media as one undo step. Proxies only change what preview, scrub and playback decode: transforms, masks, effects and text are resolution independent, and exports ALWAYS read the full-resolution media. Returns queued ids and skipped items with reasons; poll list_proxies for status.

tools.name: attach_proxies
tools.description: Attach existing proxy files that are already imported into the project to their full-resolution media (Project panel > Proxies > Attach proxies). Pass pairs [{mediaId, proxyMediaId}], or omit pairs to match by file name (extension and _proxy / -proxy suffixes ignored). Each proxy is validated against the original: it must decode, keep the aspect ratio, match the duration within 0.25 s / 1 % and the frame rate within 0.5 fps; mismatches are reported and skipped. All accepted proxies are linked as ONE undo step. The proxy media items stay in the library (delete them separately if unwanted). Exports still use full resolution.

tools.name: toggle_proxies
tools.description: Toggle Proxies (Program monitor button, Shift+P): on = preview, scrub and playback decode proxies where they exist; off = they decode the full-resolution media. Pass on=true/false to set it explicitly, or omit to flip it. Not an edit: no undo step. Export is unaffected and always uses full resolution.

tools.name: list_proxies
tools.description: Report the proxy state of every video: none | ready | building | failed | missing-proxy (link exists but the proxy bytes are gone) | missing-full (the full-resolution media is offline), its proxy resolution, build progress, whether Toggle Proxies is on and the project's ingest preset. Read-only.

tools.name: set_ingest_preset
tools.description: Set the project's ingest preset: none (default) or proxies (build proxies in the background for every video imported from now on). On the desktop app copy is also available: copy imported media into the project's Media folder (checksum-verified, originals never deleted). One undo step. Existing media is not touched; use create_proxies / copy_media_to_project for that.

tools.name: set_proxy_format
tools.description: Desktop app only. Set the project's native proxy settings (Project panel > Proxies): codec prores-proxy (ProRes 422 Proxy .mov) or h264 (.mp4), size half | quarter | 720p | 1080p (a fixed height never upscales), jobs at once 1-2, the Proxies folder and Media folder (absolute, or relative to the project file's folder; default Proxies/ and Media/ beside the project), and proxiesWithCopy (also build proxies when the copy preset ingests media). Only the fields you pass change. One undo step. Affects proxies built from now on; use create_proxies with force to rebuild.

tools.name: retry_failed_proxies
tools.description: Desktop app only (Project panel > Proxies > Retry failed). Re-queue every proxy build that failed in this project. Returns how many were retried; poll list_proxies for status.

tools.name: copy_media_to_project
tools.description: Desktop app only. Copy media files into the project's Media folder and point the project at the copies. Every copy is verified by SHA-256 (the copy is re-read and compared) and the originals are never modified or deleted. mediaIds picks items (default: every online item not yet copied). The whole batch is ONE undo step for the reference change (undo re-points to the originals; the copied files stay on disk). The project must be saved first so its Media folder has a home.

tools.name: relink_media
tools.description: Desktop app only (Project panel: Reconnect full resolution / Find proxies). Search a folder (recursively, hidden folders skipped) for offline media (kind full, default) or missing proxies (kind proxy) and relink every match by file name + duration (0.25 s / 1 %) + frame rate. A media item that two files fit equally well is reported as ambiguous and left alone. Returns linked, ambiguous, notFound and failed items.

tools.name: track_motion
tools.description: Follow a target through a video or image clip (Inspector > Motion Tracking > Start Tracking). clipId is the SOURCE clip; region {x,y,width,height} is the target in SOURCE pixels at anchorFrame (omit for the central half of the frame). Without anchorFrame the whole clip is tracked forward from frame 0. With anchorFrame (clip-local frame at project fps) set direction forward or backward to track from that frame; merge:true keeps the rest of an existing path (re-track part of it). The tracker measures per-frame confidence, re-finds the target against its reference appearance after drift, predicts through occlusion with its last velocity (those frames are reported as lost), and resumes when the target returns. Returns frames, lostFrames, lowConfidence runs, manualFrames and frames/s. Stored on the clip as ONE undo step; anything already attached follows the new path. Use attach_track to make a clip, text, shape, sticker or svg follow it.

tools.name: attach_track
tools.description: Make a clip, text, shape, sticker or svg follow a tracked path (Inspector > Motion Tracking > Apply Tracking). clipId is the tracked SOURCE clip (run track_motion first); targetId is what should move. mode follow (default) moves the target by the path's movement; pin places it on the tracked point plus offset {x,y} in project pixels. applyScale / applyRotation (default true) also follow the target's size and turn; smoothing 0..10 averages the path. Writes position/scale/rotation keyframes on the target as ONE undo step, and re-running it updates the same attachment.

tools.name: correct_track_point
tools.description: Set the tracked point at one frame by hand (Inspector > Motion Tracking > Set point). clipId is the tracked source clip, frame is clip-local at project fps, x and y are SOURCE pixels. The point becomes full confidence and is no longer counted as lost; anything attached follows. ONE undo step. Use get_motion_track to find low-confidence frames first.

tools.name: get_motion_track
tools.description: Summarise the saved motion track of a source clip: frame range, how many frames are low confidence, the runs of hidden or weak frames (candidates for track_motion with anchorFrame + merge, or correct_track_point), hand-set frames and the first and last point. Returns null data when the clip has no valid track (never tracked, or its source changed).

tools.name: get_audio_latency_report
tools.description: Report the processing latency of lookahead/FFT audio effects (compressor, limiter, DeClick, DeClip, DeReverb and the zero-latency repair effects) and what the project's mixer adds. data.effects lists each effect's latency in samples and ms; data.tracks lists each track's rack latency and the compensation delay the graph inserts so parallel tracks and buses stay aligned; data.totalLatencyMs is how late the whole mix leaves the graph before offline renders and the realtime scheduler compensate it. Compensation is automatic, so a click stays on the same sample as the picture; this is for diagnosing and explaining. Read-only.

tools.name: analyze_audio_issues
tools.description: Analyze a clip's audio (as it sounds before any repair effects) for mains hum (50/60 Hz and harmonics), clipping, clicks and harsh sibilance. Returns data.report (hum {present, frequency, prominenceDb, harmonics}, clipping {present, runs, clippedSamples, peak}, clicks {present, count, perMinute}, sibilance {present, centerHz, thresholdDb, fraction}, peakDb) and data.suggestions: the repair effects (type + params + reason) that would address what was found. Read-only; needs the live editor's audio decoder. Use add_audio_repair to apply.

tools.name: add_audio_repair
tools.description: Add repair effects to a clip as ONE undo step. auto:true (the default when no fixes are given) analyzes the clip and adds only what it found (hum, clipping, clicks, sibilance), with the suggested settings. fixes: explicit effect types to add (deHum | deClick | deClip | deEss | deReverb | gate | brickwallLimiter | lowPass) with their default or given params (params: {deHum: {frequency: 50, harmonics: 4}, deEss: {threshold: -28}}; ranges in get_capabilities / the effect definitions: deHum frequency 40-70 Hz, harmonics 1-8, q 5-100, depth 0-1; deClick sensitivity 0-1, maxWidth 2-48 samples; deClip threshold -24..0 dBFS, maxRun 4-120; deEss frequency 2500-12000 Hz, threshold -60..0 dB, ratio 1-20, listen 0/1; deReverb amount 0-1, rt60 0.1-3 s, floor -40..0 dB; gate threshold -80..0 dB, range -80..0 dB, hold 0-1 s; brickwallLimiter ceiling -24..0 dBTP, release 0.01-1 s (5 ms lookahead, true-peak safe); lowPass frequency 100-20000 Hz, slope 12-48 dB/oct). A repair effect already on the clip is updated instead of duplicated. DeReverb is experimental (reduces the late tail only, adds ~21 ms latency). The same effects can sit on a track/bus rack via set_track_audio_rack. Returns data.added with each effect id, type, params and reason.

tools.name: queue_stems_export
tools.description: Add a stems job to the export queue (Export queue panel > Stems) and, unless start=false, start the queue. The job snapshots the project now; when it runs it renders each selected bus (busIds; default every bus that carries audio) as its own WAV through the export mixdown, all full-length and sample-aligned so they re-sum in a DAW, and bundles them in one zip. bitDepth 16 or 24 (default 24); filename overrides the zip name. Returns data.jobId; poll list_export_jobs, where a finished stems job lists data.jobs[].stems (one entry per WAV with fileName, bytes, durationSec). Not an edit: no undo step. Expensive - requires confirmation.

tools.name: list_effect_params
tools.description: List the animatable numeric parameters of one effect instance on a clip (key, label, min, max, step, current value) with their instance keyframes (time, value, easing). Use the keys with set_effect_param_keyframe.

tools.name: set_effect_param_keyframe
tools.description: Add or update a keyframe on one numeric parameter of one effect INSTANCE at a clip-local time in seconds (the inspector stopwatch). Keyframes belong to the instance, so two copies of the same effect animate independently. Works for every classic video effect; see list_effect_params for the keys. A keyframe already at that time is updated. One undo step.

tools.name: remove_effect_param_keyframe
tools.description: Remove the keyframe of an effect instance parameter at a clip-local time (seconds), or every keyframe of that parameter when time is omitted (stopwatch off; the parameter keeps its stored value). One undo step.

tools.name: duplicate_video_effect
tools.description: Duplicate an effect instance on a clip, inserted right after the original, together with its parameter keyframes (the copy animates independently from then on). Returns the new effectId. One undo step.

tools.name: list_effect_presets
tools.description: List the project's saved effect presets (id, name, timing mode, effect types, keyframe count).

tools.name: save_effect_preset
tools.description: Save effects of a clip (all of them, or only effectIds) with their parameter keyframes as a named preset in the project. timing 'relative' (default) stores keyframe times as a fraction of the clip duration so the animation stretches to the clip it is applied to; 'absolute' keeps seconds. Returns presetId. One undo step.

tools.name: apply_effect_preset
tools.description: Apply a saved effect preset to a clip: its effects are added as fresh independent instances with their keyframes (relative presets are scaled to this clip's duration). mode 'append' (default) adds to the stack, 'replace' replaces the clip's effect stack. Returns the new effectIds. One undo step.

tools.name: delete_effect_preset
tools.description: Delete a saved effect preset (clips that already used it keep their effects). One undo step.

tools.name: export_effect_presets
tools.description: Return saved effect presets as JSON text (all, or only presetIds) in the portable OpenReel preset file format, for sharing or backup. Import with import_effect_presets.

tools.name: import_effect_presets
tools.description: Import effect presets from JSON text produced by export_effect_presets (or a single preset object). The file is validated strictly; presets are added to the project library and never overwrite existing ones. Returns the new presetIds. One undo step.
